ref_atoms.ref_content: Interrupt kmac_done: KMAC/SHA3 absorbing has been completed.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific interrupt kmac_done with clear condition of absorbing completion.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Interrupt fifo_empty: raised when the message FIFO is empty, but only if all of the following conditions are met: i) The KMAC block is not exercised by a hardware application interface. ii) The SHA3 block is in the Absorb state. iii) Software has not yet written the Process command to finish the absorption process. For the interrupt to be raised, the message FIFO must also have been full previously. Otherwise, the hardware empties the FIFO faster than software can fill it and there is no point in interrupting the software.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific interrupt fifo_empty with detailed conditions involving MSG_FIFO, Process command, Absorb state.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Interrupt kmac_err: KMAC/SHA3 error occurred. ERR_CODE register shows the details.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific interrupt kmac_err linked to ERR_CODE register for error details.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Alert recov_operation_err: occurs when the shadow registers have update errors.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific alert recov_operation_err triggered by shadow register update errors.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Alert fatal_fault_err: triggered when a fatal error is detected inside the KMAC unit. Examples include: i) TL-UL bus integrity fault. ii) Storage errors in the shadow registers. iii) Errors in the message, round, or key counter. iv) Any internal FSM entering an invalid state. v) An error in the redundant lfsr. The KMAC unit cannot recover from such an error and needs to be reset.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific alert fatal_fault_err listing concrete internal fault sources (shadow regs, counters, FSM, lfsr).

ref_atoms.ref_content: The global escalation input signal lc_escalate_en from the life cycle is multibit encoded (MUBI).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific signal lc_escalate_en required to be multibit encoded.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Data storage and secret key are two share to guard against 1st order attack.
Round counter, key index counter, sentmsg counter and hash counter use prim_count for redundancy.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific counters (round, key index, sentmsg, hash) using prim_count for redundancy.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Packer Position counter uses prim_count for redundancy.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific Packer Position counter using prim_count for redundancy.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Escalation moves all sparse FSMs into an invalid state.
Local fatal faults move all sparse FSMs into an invalid state.
The reset net for the internal state register and critical nets around the output register are buried.
`absorbed` signal is mubi4_t type to protect against FI attacks.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific signal `absorbed` enforced as mubi4_t type.

ref_atoms.ref_content: `sw_cmd` and related signals are sparse encoded to protect against FI attacks.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific signal `sw_cmd` and related signals are sparse encoded.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KMAC supports SHA3 hashing algorithm with security strength configurations: SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512. Compliant with NIST FIPS 202.
KMAC supports SHAKE hashing algorithm with security strength configurations: SHAKE128, SHAKE256. Compliant with NIST FIPS 202.
KMAC supports cSHAKE hashing algorithm with security strength configurations: cSHAKE128, cSHAKE256. Compliant with NIST SP 800-185.
KMAC supports KMAC Keccak Message Authentication Code with security strength configurations: KMAC128, KMAC256. Compliant with NIST SP 800-185.
SHAKE, cSHAKE and KMAC modes of operation support eXtendable-Output Format (XOF) as specified in NIST SP 800-185.
Configurable input message endianness.
Configurable output digest endianness.
Key can be loaded directly from the keymgr.

Entropy required for countermeasures can be configured to be provided by software or EDN. In EDN mode, KMAC can be configured to set an error flag if entropy is not provided within a configurable time window. The cadence of entropy requested from EDN is also configurable.

CFG_REGWEN register controls the configurability of CFG_SHADOWED register. This register ensures that the contents of CFG_SHADOWED cannot be changed by software while the KMAC/SHA3 is in operation mode. Field en: Configuration enable (read-only, HW managed).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register CFG_REGWEN with explicit behavior: gates writes to CFG_SHADOWED during operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CFG_SHADOWED register is updated when the hashing engine is in Idle. If software updates the register while the engine computes, the updated value will be discarded. It is shadowed with update_err_alert=recov_operation_err and storage_err_alert=fatal_fault_err. Fields: kmac_en (bit0) - if 1, incoming message is processed in KMAC with secret key. kstrength (bits3:1) - selects security strength; invalid value results in error when hashing starts. mode (bits5:4) - selects Keccak mode (SHA3, SHAKE, cSHAKE). msg_endianness (bit8) - if 1, multi-byte values written to MSG_FIFO are added to the message in big-endian byte order; 0 little-endian. state_endianness (bit9) - if 1, each word in STATE register is converted to big-endian byte order. sideload (bit12) - if 1, KMAC uses KeyMgr sideloaded key for SW initiated KMAC operation. entropy_mode (bits17:16) - configures PRNG mode: idle_mode (default after reset, cannot return once switched), edn_mode (requests entropy from EDN after entropy_ready, periodic reseeding via ENTROPY_PERIOD), sw_mode (waits for software to write ENTROPY_SEED registers exactly once and in ascending order). entropy_fast_process (bit19) - if 1, entropy logic uses garbage data while not processing the KMAC key block. msg_mask (bit20) - if 1, KMAC applies PRNG to input messages in KMAC mode. entropy_ready (bit24) - set by software to allow entropy generator to fetch entropy and run. en_unsupported_modestrength (bit26) - if set, KMAC proceeds with unsupported Mode/Strength configurations.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register CFG_SHADOWED with detailed field behaviors (operation gating, mode, endianness, entropy control).

ref_atoms.ref_content: CMD register controls the KMAC/SHA3 operation sequence: start --> process --> {run if needed -->} done. Fields: cmd (bits5:0) sparse encoded commands: start (29) begins operation when idle; before receiving message, processes Function name N and customization S if cSHAKE, and secret key block if KMAC. process (46) computes digest/signing after receiving entire message. run (49) triggers full 24 Keccak rounds during squeeze (optional). done (22) clears internal variables and returns to Idle. entropy_req (bit8) software triggered entropy request. hash_cnt_clr (bit9) clears the hash counter in entropy module. err_processed (bit10) lets FSM return to reset state after error handling.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register CMD with explicit command sequence and per-command behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: STATUS register provides KMAC/SHA3 state. Fields: sha3_idle (bit0) - 1 if SHA3 engine idle. sha3_absorb (bit1) - 1 if receiving/processing message. sha3_squeeze (bit2) - 1 if sponge absorbing completed, SW can manually run engine. fifo_depth (bits12:8) - occupied entries in message FIFO. fifo_empty (bit14) - message FIFO empty indicator; due to pass-through mode, fifo_depth stays 0 but fifo_empty toggles low for a cycle then returns high. fifo_full (bit15) - message FIFO full indicator. ALERT_FATAL_FAULT (bit16) - 1 if a fatal fault occurred (bus integrity, shadow storage, counter, FSM, lfsr errors). ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR (bit17) - 1 if an update error occurred in the shadowed Control Register.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register STATUS with detailed behavior of each status bit including fifo_empty pass-through behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: ENTROPY_PERIOD register configures entropy wait timer. prescaler (bits9:0) - EDN wait timer prescaler; a timer pulse is generated when the number of clock cycles hits this prescaler value. wait_timer (bits31:16) - EDN request wait timer; the entropy module waits up to this value in timer pulses after sending request to EDN. If the timer expires, the module moves to an error state. If wait_timer is 0, the module waits indefinitely. Pending EDN requests during wait timer update are delayed until completion.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register ENTROPY_PERIOD with clear prescaler and wait timer behavior including error state on timeout.

ref_atoms.ref_content: ENTROPY_REFRESH_HASH_CNT register holds the hash (KMAC) counter. If this counter reaches (GTE) the configured ENTROPY_REFRESH_THRESHOLD_SHADOWED, the entropy module requests a new seed from EDN and resets the counter. If threshold is 0, refresh by counter does not work and the counter is only reset by CMD.hash_cnt_clr.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register ENTROPY_REFRESH_HASH_CNT with behavior: triggers entropy refresh on reaching threshold.

ref_atoms.ref_content: ENTROPY_REFRESH_THRESHOLD_SHADOWED register sets the threshold for entropy refresh. When the hash counter ENTROPY_REFRESH_HASH_CNT reaches (GTE) this threshold, the entropy module requests a new seed from EDN and resets the hash counter. If threshold is 0, refresh by counter is disabled, and the counter is only reset via CMD.hash_cnt_clr. It is shadowed with update_err_alert=recov_operation_err and storage_err_alert=fatal_fault_err.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register ENTROPY_REFRESH_THRESHOLD_SHADOWED with refresh behavior and shadow error alerts.

ref_atoms.ref_content: ENTROPY_SEED register is used when CFG_SHADOWED.entropy_mode is set to sw_mode. After setting CFG_SHADOWED.entropy_ready, software writes the ENTROPY_SEED register 9 times. Each write loads the value into a chunk of the entropy generator state. After 9 writes, the entropy generator starts operation and further writes have no effect.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register ENTROPY_SEED with exact sw_mode seeding sequence (9 writes).

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEY_SHARE0 registers (NumWordsKey entries) hold the first share of the KMAC secret key (up to 512 bits). Key ordering: key[512:0] = {KEY15, KEY14, ... , KEY0}. The registers may only be updated when the engine is in Idle state. If the engine computes the hash, any update attempt is discarded and an error is reported. Upper bits of the secret key must be kept 0.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register KEY_SHARE0 with write protection during computation and key ordering.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEY_SHARE1 registers (NumWordsKey entries) hold the second share of the KMAC secret key (up to 512 bits). Same write restrictions apply as KEY_SHARE0: only updatable when idle; updates during computation are discarded and reported as error. Upper bits must be kept 0.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register KEY_SHARE1 with write protection during computation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEY_LEN register selects the secret key length in bits. Supports 128b, 192b, 256b, 384b, and 512b (enum values). This value is used to encode the secret key in KMAC. Only updatable when the engine is idle (regwen: CFG_REGWEN).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register KEY_LEN with defined key length options and write protection.

ref_atoms.ref_content: PREFIX registers (NumWordsPrefix entries) hold the cSHAKE prefix containing Function Name N and Customization String S, encoded as encode_string(N) || encode_string(S) || 0. Software must fill the register with the encoded value per NIST SP 800-185 Section 2.3.2. The registers may only be updated when the engine is in Idle; updates during computation are discarded and an error is reported.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register PREFIX with string encoding requirement and write protection during computation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: ERR_CODE register holds error information when the kmac_err interrupt occurs. Bits 31:24 contain the error code (see err_code_e encoding), and bits 23:0 contain additional debug information. This register does not get cleared when the kmac_err interrupt state is cleared.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register ERR_CODE providing error code and debug info on kmac_err, with not-cleared-on-interrupt-clear behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: STATE memory window (0x400 - 0x4C7 for state share, 0x500 - 0x5C7 for mask share) provides read-only access to the 1600-bit Keccak state. Software reads the processed digest from this region. If masking is enabled (EnMasking=1), two shares are read; otherwise the mask share returns 0.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific STATE window with dual-share access depending on EnMasking parameter.

ref_atoms.ref_content: MSG_FIFO window (2kB range at 0x800) is a write-only message FIFO. Any write to this address range appends data to the FIFO. Internal hardware handles byte/word packing; the least significant 12 address bits are ignored. The FIFO's pass-through mode means that when the SHA engine is ready, write data passes through, keeping fifo_depth at 0 while fifo_empty toggles low for a cycle.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific MSG_FIFO window with pass-through behavior affecting fifo_empty and fifo_depth.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Countermeasure sec_cm_lc_escalate_en_intersig_mubi: Verify global LC_ESCALATE_EN mubi.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific signal LC_ESCALATE_EN with mubi encoding for verification.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Countermeasure sec_cm_key_sideload: Verify the key from KeyMgr is sideloaded.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Key sideloading from KeyMgr is a specific hardware behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KMAC smoke test runs a full hashing operation: randomize interrupts, mode, key length, endianness; set function name 'KMAC', customization empty; set output length; select entropy source; during absorption, read from STATE window expect 0; write message (max 32 bytes); check status and kmac_done, status.squeeze set; read digest and compare with C model (XOR shares for masked, share2=0 for unmasked); issue cmd.done to clear state, read digest again confirm 0; DPI-C and scoreboard check correctness.
Same as smoke but with message up to 100KB and output length up to 1KB for XOF; manually run keccak rounds to squeeze extra output; randomize function name 'KMAC' and customization string.
Burst-write chunks of the message into msg_fifo, disable intermediate status/CSR checks, similar to long_message test.
Drive NIST test vectors for SHA3/SHAKE/KMAC; check output digest against expected values.
Set cfg.sideload and provide a valid sideloaded key along with a valid SW-provided key; KMAC should operate on the sideloaded key regardless of cfg_shadowed.sideload field value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Points to cfg.sideload and cfg_shadowed.sideload registers and describes hardware behavior of using sideloaded key regardless of shadowed field.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Keymgr/ROM/LC initiate KMAC operation via application interface; use kmac_app_agents to send message and control hashing; set cfg.sideload if Keymgr enabled; compare digest with DPI model; read from STATE window afterwards, confirm access blocked and returns 0.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Checks STATE window access blocked returning 0 after app operation, a specific hardware mechanism.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Based on app test, send partial data via application interface with strb values other than 8'hFF; will not check status and intr_state registers but will check other registers and interface digest; scoreboard not cycle-accurate for this.

Test entropy interface: randomly select SW or App hash; request EDN entropy via cmd.entropy_req, cmd.hash_cnt_clear, and entropy_refresh_threshold_shadowed; in masked mode check entropy_refresh_hash_cnt value and EDN request timing; in unmasked mode check entropy_refresh_hash_cnt always 0.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Tests entropy_refresh_hash_cnt register behavior and EDN request timing with masked/unmasked modes.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Try several error sequences: update key/prefix/config during absorption/process/squeeze; write msg to msg_fifo during process/squeeze; in KMAC mode, set function name not 'KMAC'; incorrect SHA3 control flow (e.g., Process before Start, Run before Process); incorrect KMAC configurations; provide SW inputs during app operation.

Test KMAC response when Keymgr app sends request but key not valid: configure KMAC, send keymgr request without setting valid bit; wait, issue err_processed, wait for handshake finish; repeat. Check err_code, status, interrupt; check keymgr interface response with all-zero digests and error bit set; check KMAC resumes normal operation afterwards.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Checks err_code, status, interrupt registers and keymgr interface error bit for key not valid scenario.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Invalidate sideloaded key by forcing .valid signal to 0 during random app state; check err_code; check keymgr interface response with all-zero digests and error bit set; check KMAC resumes normal operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Checks err_code and keymgr interface response when sideloaded key valid signal forced to 0.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Configure EDN timeout error by writing entropy_period.wait_timer and entropy_period.prescaler; check err_code, status, interrupt; check keymgr interface error bit set; check KMAC resumes; timeout not triggered if entropy_mode is SW or masking disabled.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Checks EDN timeout error registers and conditions: entropy_period registers, err_code, status, interrupt, and interaction with entropy_mode/masking.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Write incorrect ral.cfg_shadowed.entropy_mode before entropy fetch; check err_code, status, interrupt; check keymgr interface error bit set; check KMAC resumes; timeout not triggered if masking disabled.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Checks err_code, status, interrupt and keymgr interface for incorrect entropy_mode configuration.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Do not write 1 to ral.cfg_shadowed.entropy_ready before KMAC operation; if masking enabled and EDN mode: for SW operation check err_code, status, interrupt; for APP operation check keymgr interface error bit; if masking disabled or no entropy required, no error.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Checks err_code, status, interrupt or keymgr interface based on entropy_ready setting and masking/EDN mode.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Set lc_escalate_en to non-Off during KMAC operations; check fatal alert fires continuously until reset; status.alert_fatal_fault set to 1, sha3_idle reset to 0; KMAC does not accept any SW or APP requests; Digest window always outputs 0.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Checks fatal alert, alert_fatal_fault, sha3_idle, and digest window behavior when lc_escalate_en is active.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Combine above sequences in one test sequentially (except csr sequence and some error tests that disabled scoreboard), with random reset between sequences.
Measure throughput of various hashing calculations and ensure they correspond to expected throughput range.
Cover all valid configuration settings: hashing mode (sha3/shake/kmac), security strength, key length, message/digest endianness, XOF mode when KMAC; crossing all valid combinations.
Cover various input message length ranges from 0 bytes to 10,000 bytes, including corner cases (length 0).
Cover various output digest lengths for XOF functions to ensure KMAC can produce outputs of varying sizes.
Cover that prefix values (function_name + customization_string) consist of valid alphabet letters or space.
Cover that msgfifo has been written using all possible TLUL masks.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers msgfifo write behavior with all TLUL masks, a specific hardware interface feature.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover all possible fifo statuses during different hash operations: various depths, fifo full, fifo empty.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers msgfifo statuses (full, empty, depth) during different hash operations, a specific hardware buffer state.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that all sha3-related status fields have eventually been seen.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers all sha3-related status fields, specific hardware status signals.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that state windows have been read using all possible TLUL masks.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers state window read behavior with all TLUL masks, a specific hardware access feature.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that KMAC handles CmdProcess command during various msgfifo status (full/empty/in between) and while keccak rounds are active/inactive.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers CmdProcess command handling under specific msgfifo status and keccak round states, a specific hardware control flow.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover scenarios where sideloaded key is provided and should be used (en_sideload==1, app_mode==AppKeymgr) and where sideloaded key is provided but should not be used.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers sideloaded key usage conditions with en_sideload and app_mode, a specific hardware configuration.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover app interface scenarios: single data beat, all partial data lengths (last beat), errors reported through interface, Done signal while keccak rounds active/inactive.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers app interface scenarios with Done signal and keccak rounds, specific hardware control and error reporting.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover app interface and cfg_shadowed register: hash_mode, kmac_en, kstrength; SW register settings should not affect app interface calculation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers cfg_shadowed register fields effect on app interface, a specific hardware configuration interaction.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover values for entropy_period register's prescaler and wait_timer fields, crossed with EDN mode on/off.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers entropy_period register prescaler/wait_timer and EDN mode, a specific hardware timer configuration.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover all error scenarios: ErrKeyNotValid, ErrSwPushedMsgFifo, ErrSwIssuedCmdInAppActive, ErrWaitTimerExpired, ErrIncorrectEntropyMode, ErrUnexpectedModeStrength, ErrIncorrectFunctionName, ErrSwCmdSequence.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Covers specific error codes generated by hardware under defined conditions.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The MSG_FIFO has a packer in front. It packs any partial writes into the size of internal datapath (64bit) and stores in MSG_FIFO. It frees the software from having to align the messages. It also doesn't need the message length information.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names MSG_FIFO packer and describes its packing behavior to 64-bit, providing a testable assertion.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The fed messages go into the KMAC core regardless of KMAC enabled or not. The KMAC core forwards the messages to SHA3 core in case KMAC hash functionality is disabled. KMAC core prepends the encoded secret key as described in the SHA3 Derived Functions specification.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes KMAC core message forwarding and prepending behavior depending on KMAC_en, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If cSHAKE mode is set, the padding logic also prepends the encoded function name N and the customization string S prior to the incoming messages according to the spec requirements.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Identifies cSHAKE padding logic prepending N and S, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Both the internal state width and the masking of the Keccak core are configurable via compile-time Verilog parameters. By default, 1600 bits of internal state are used and stored in two shares (1st order masking). The masked Keccak core takes 4 clock cycles per round if sufficient entropy is available. If desired, the masking can be disabled and the internal state width can be reduced to 25, 50, or 100 bits at compile time.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: States masked Keccak core cycle count and state width configurability, directly testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Keccak permutations in the specification allow arbitrary number of rounds. This module, however, supports Keccak_f which always runs 12 + 2*L rounds, where L = log2(Width/25).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies exact round count formula, testable for different Width values.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the compile-time Verilog parameter EnMasking is not set, i.e., if masking is not enabled, the first phase and the second phase run at the same cycle.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies unmasked Keccak round phase execution in a single cycle, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If masking is enabled, the Keccak round logic stores the intermediate state after processing the 1st phase, then feeds to the 2nd phase computing Chi and Iota. The Chi function uses 800 DOM multipliers, fully pipelined, and the 2nd phase takes three clock cycles: first cycle computes first lane halves, second cycle outputs them and starts second lane halves, third cycle outputs second lane halves. The 800 DOM multipliers need 800 bits of fresh entropy for remasking; if not available, the DOM multipliers stall and the 2nd phase takes more than three cycles. Processing a Keccak_f (1600 bit state) takes 96 cycles (24 rounds x 4 cycles/round). The masked round logic requires an additional 3200 flip flops and two sets of Theta, Rho, Pi functions.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Details masked Keccak round phases, DOM multiplier pipeline, entropy dependency, and total cycles, all directly testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If cSHAKE is enabled, the padding logic expands the prefix value (N || S) into a block size. The block size is determined by CFG_SHADOWED.kstrength: if the value is 128, the block size will be 168 bytes; if it is 256, the block size will be 136 bytes. After sending the block size, the padding logic triggers the Keccak round logic to run a full 24 rounds.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies cSHAKE prefix expansion block size dependent on CFG_SHADOWED.kstrength and the resulting trigger of Keccak rounds, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: After the software writes the message bitstream, it should issue the Process command into CMD register. The padding logic, after receiving the Process command, appends proper ending bits with respect to the CFG_SHADOWED.mode value. The logic writes 0 up to the block size to the Keccak round logic then ends with 1 at the end of the block.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes padding logic behavior after Process command, appending 0…1 ending bits, dependent on CFG_SHADOWED.mode, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: After the Keccak round completes the last block, the padding logic asserts an absorbed signal to notify the software. The signal generates the kmac_done interrupt.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names absorbed signal and its generation of kmac_done interrupt, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the output length is greater than the Keccak block rate in SHAKE and cSHAKE mode, the software may run the Keccak round manually by issuing Run command to CMD register.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies manual Run command support for SHAKE/cSHAKE when output exceeds block rate, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The software completes the operation by issuing Done command. The padding logic clears internal variables and goes back to Idle state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes Done command effect on padding logic FSM, clearing variables and returning to Idle, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KMAC core prepends a block containing the encoded secret key to the output message. The KMAC first sends the block of secret key then accepts the incoming message bitstream.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes KMAC padding prepend of secret key block and the ordering of message acceptance, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: At the end of the message, the software writes right_encode(output_length) to MSG_FIFO prior to issue Process command.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies requirement to write right_encode(output_length) to MSG_FIFO before Process command, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The depth of the message FIFO is chosen to cover the throughput. Default design parameters assume: RegLatency: register write takes 5 cycles, Sha3Latency: masked Keccak round latency takes 96 cycles.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Provides the latency assumptions (5 cycles register write, 96 cycles Keccak) used for FIFO depth calculation, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the SW is slow and the SHA3 engine pops the data fast enough, the Message FIFO's depth may remain 0. The Message FIFO's fifo_empty status bit, however, is lowered for a cycle.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes fifo_empty status bit behavior even when FIFO depth is 0, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the SHA3 engine is currently busy or if the KMAC block is waiting for fresh entropy from EDN, the Message FIFO may actually run full (indicated by the fifo_full status bit). The fifo_empty status interrupt will not fire if i) one of the hardware application interfaces is using the KMAC block, ii) the SHA3 core is not in the Absorb state, or iii) after software has written the Process command.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies conditions under which fifo_full asserts and when fifo_empty interrupt is suppressed, directly testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If either the entropy wait timer is nonzero or kmac_en is false (so KMAC will not be refreshing entropy), it is safe to write to the FIFO without polling STATUS.fifo_depth.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Identifies hardware conditions (entropy timer nonzero or kmac_en false) under which FIFO writes are safe without depth polling, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The message FIFO does not generate the masked message data. Incoming message bitstream is not sensitive to the leakage. If the EnMasking parameter is set and CFG_SHADOWED.msg_mask is enabled, the message is masked upon loading into the Keccak core using the internal entropy generator.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies that message masking occurs at Keccak core load time only when EnMasking and msg_mask are set, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The secret key is stored as masked form always.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: States constant masked storage for secret key, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the EnMasking parameter is not set, the masking is disabled. Then, the software has to provide the key in unmasked form by default. Any write operations to KEY_SHARE1_0 - KEY_SHARE1_15 are ignored.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes unmasked key requirement and ignoring of KEY_SHARE1 writes when EnMasking is disabled, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the EnMasking parameter is not set and the SwKeyMasked parameter is set, software has to provide the key in masked form. Internally, the design then unmasks the key by XORing the two key shares together when loading the key into the engine.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes SwKeyMasked mode when EnMasking is disabled, requiring masked key input and internal XOR unmasking, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the EnMasking parameter is set, the SwKeyMasked parameter has no effect: Software always provides the key in two shares.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies that with EnMasking enabled, SwKeyMasked is ignored and two share key is mandatory, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If the compile-time parameter masking feature is enabled, the upper 256B of the window is the second share of the Keccak state. If not, the upper address space is zero value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines state window mapping for masked shares, testable by reading upper 256B.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The Keccak state is valid after the sponge absorbing process is completed. While in an idle state or in the sponge absorbing stage, the value is zero. This ensures that the logic does not expose the secret key XORed with the keccak_f results of the prefix to the software.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes Keccak state validity and zeroing behavior to prevent exposure, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The KMAC/SHA3 blocks the software access to the Keccak state when it processes the request from KeyMgr for KDF.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies that Keccak state access is blocked during KDF requests from KeyMgr, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The software should set CFG_SHADOWED.sideload to use the KeyMgr sideloaded key. KeyMgr provides the sideloaded key in two-share masked form regardless of EnMasking. If EnMasking is not defined, the KMAC merges the shared key to the unmasked form before uses the key.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes sideload key usage, its always two-share form, and merging when EnMasking absent, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The state machine inside the AppIntf logic starts when it receives the first valid data from any of the AppIntf. The AppIntf module chooses the winner based on the fixed priority. Then it forwards the selected App to the next stage. Because this logic sees the first valid data as an initiator, the Apps cannot run the hashing operation with an empty message.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies AppIntf FSM start condition, fixed priority arbitration, and empty message limitation, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: After the logic switches to accept the message bitstream from the selected App, if the hashing operation is KMAC, the logic forces the sideloaded key to be used as a secret. Also it ignores the command issued from the software. Instead it generates the commands and sends them to the KMAC core.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes AppIntf forcing sideload key and ignoring SW commands during KMAC app operation, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The last beat of the App data moves the state machine to append the encoded output length if the hashing operation is KMAC. The output length is the digest width, which is 256 bit always. The logic appends 0x020100 (little-endian) to the end of the message. The output data goes to MSG_FIFO. Because the MSG_FIFO handles un-aligned data inside, the KeyMgr interface logic sends the encoded output length value in a separate beat. After the encoded output length is pushed to the KMAC core, the interface logic issues a Process command to run the hashing logic.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Details AppIntf's automatic appending of encoded output length (0x020100) for KMAC, separate beat over MSG_FIFO, and subsequent Process command, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: After hashing operation is completed, KMAC does not raise a kmac_done interrupt; rather it triggers the done status in the App response channel. The result digest always comes in two shares. If the EnMasking parameter is not set, the second share is always zero.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies application completion signaling via done channel rather than kmac_done, and digest sharing behavior, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The entropy generator is constructed using a heavily unrolled Bivium stream cipher primitive. This allows the module to generate 800 bits of fresh, pseudo-random numbers required by the 800 DOM multipliers for remasking in every clock cycle.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes entropy generator construction and its capability to produce 800 bits per cycle for DOM remasking, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Depending on CFG_SHADOWED.entropy_mode, the entropy generator fetches initial entropy from the EDN module or software has to provide a seed by writing the ENTROPY_SEED register 9 times.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies entropy source selection (EDN or SW seed via ENTROPY_SEED x 9) based on entropy_mode, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The module periodically refreshes the PRNG seed with fresh entropy from EDN. Software can explicitly request a complete reseed of the PRNG state from EDN through CMD.entropy_req.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes periodic EDN refresh and SW-triggered reseed via CMD.entropy_req, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KeyNotValid error (0x01): When a KMAC application requests a hashing operation, the module checks if the sideloaded key is ready. If not ready, it reports the error and moves to dead-end state, waiting for IP reset.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific error with clear trigger (sideload key not ready) and response (dead-end state), testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SwPushedMsgFifo error (0x02): Occurs when the Message FIFO receives TL-UL transactions while the application interface is busy. The request is dropped. The IP reports error with info: bits [15:8] kmac_app_st (KMAC_APP FSM state), [7:0] mux_sel (current APP Mux selection: 0=None, 1=SW, 2=App).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes error condition, response (drop request), and debug info fields, all testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SwIssuedCmdInAppActive error (0x03): If SW issues any commands while the application interface is being used, the module reports error. The command does not affect the Application process and is dropped by KMAC_APP. The lower 3 bits of ERR_CODE contain the received command.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies error on SW command during app active, dropped command, and command value in ERR_CODE bits, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: WaitTimerExpired error (0x04): Timer is used only when pending EDN request is completed; dynamic change cannot unstall. If a non-zero timer expires, the module cancels the transaction and reports error. The KMAC_ENTROPY state machine moves to Wait state, keeps using pre-generated entropy and asserting entropy valid to complete current hash. If not completed, creates back pressure on message FIFO potentially deadlocking the crossbar. SW can reset by issuing CMD.err_processed.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes timeout behavior, fallback to pre-generated entropy, potential deadlock, and SW recovery via CMD.err_processed, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: IncorrectEntropyMode error (0x05): If SW misconfigures the entropy mode and lets the entropy module prepare random data, the module reports error and moves to Wait state after reporting. SW may reset by issuing CMD.err_processed.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies error on entropy mode misconfig, Wait state, and SW recovery, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: UnexpectedModeStrength error (0x06): When SW issues Start command, KMAC_ERRCHK checks CFG_SHADOWED.mode and CFG_SHADOWED.kstrength for valid combinations (SHA3-224/256/384/512, SHAKE-128/256, cSHAKE-128/256). If combination is invalid, error is reported but the hashing operation proceeds, possibly yielding incorrect digest.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies mode/kstrength validation, error reporting, and that operation continues with potentially wrong result, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: IncorrectFunctionName error (0x07): If CFG_SHADOWED.kmac_en is set and SW issues Start, KMAC_ERRCHK checks if PREFIX has correct function name 'encode_string("KMAC")' (byte form 0x4341_4D4B_2001). If mismatch, error reported but operation continues, possibly yielding incorrect signature.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies PREFIX validation for KMAC, error reporting, and continued operation with potentially wrong signature, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SwCmdSequence error (0x08): KMAC_ERRCHK checks if SW issued commands follow the guideline. If command is not relevant to current context, error reported. The lower 3 bits of ERR_CODE contain the received command. The incorrect command is dropped at the SHA3 core.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes command sequencing check, error reporting with command code in ERR_CODE, and dropping of invalid command, testable.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Sha3Control error (0x80): SW may receive Sha3Control error along with SwCmdSequence error. This error can be ignored.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific error code with defined occurrence condition (alongside SwCmdSequence) and ignorable nature, testable.
